title: The class trip
setup_text: The class is going on a trip. The fee fits this month only if the family postpones something else your child has been looking forward to.

choices.label: Pay for the trip and postpone the plan
choices.outcome_text: Your child joined the class trip. The family made a new date for the plan that had to wait.

choices.label: Keep the family plan and skip the trip
choices.outcome_text: The family plan stayed on the calendar. Your child missed the trip and later listened to classmates tell their stories.

choices.label: Ask the school about payment options
choices.outcome_text: A conversation with school opened up more information. The family had to wait before making its plans.

title: A lift after school
setup_text: A neighbour offers to pick up your child with theirs. It would save a daily journey, but you do not know their routine well yet.

choices.label: Try the lift on one agreed day
choices.outcome_text: One afternoon became easier to plan. The family checked how the journey had gone before arranging another.

choices.label: Keep the current pickup routine
choices.outcome_text: The familiar journey stayed in place. The neighbour remained available for an occasional change of plans.

choices.label: Meet and plan the route together
choices.outcome_text: A short meeting made room for questions about the journey. The daily routine stayed as it was while everyone decided.

title: Money at the school gate
setup_text: Your child wants to buy a snack for a friend who forgot theirs. The money was meant to last the week.

choices.label: Let your child share the snack money
choices.outcome_text: The friend got a snack and there was less money for the remaining days. Your child thought about how to make it last.

choices.label: Offer to share food brought from home
choices.outcome_text: A snack from the bag was split between two children. The saved money stayed for another day.

choices.label: Talk about a small amount for sharing
choices.outcome_text: The family made a small sharing plan. It meant choosing what else the weekly money could cover.

title: The photograph of a drawing
setup_text: A relative wants to post your child’s drawing in the family group. Your child worked hard on it but has not decided who should see it.

choices.label: Ask your child before it is shared
choices.outcome_text: The drawing waited while your child chose who could see it. The relative received an answer a little later.

choices.label: Show it at the next family visit
choices.outcome_text: The picture stayed at home until the family met. There was a chance to see people’s faces as they looked at it.

choices.label: Offer to send it privately to the relative
choices.outcome_text: One person received the picture instead of the whole group. Your child kept the original on the table.

title: A Sunday invitation
setup_text: A school friend invites your child to a Sunday activity at their family’s church. Your own family usually spends that morning elsewhere.

choices.label: Let your child attend with the friend
choices.outcome_text: The morning brought new faces and songs. The family’s usual Sunday plan changed for that week.

choices.label: Invite the friend to your family’s activity
choices.outcome_text: The invitation went the other way. Your child shared a familiar place, while the friend’s original plan stayed on another calendar.

choices.label: Suggest meeting after both activities
choices.outcome_text: Both morning routines stayed in place. The children had a shorter time together later in the day.

title: Saturday on the calendar
setup_text: Your child wants to join a Saturday club. That is also when the family usually cleans and visits relatives.

choices.label: Try the club for a few weeks
choices.outcome_text: The club found a place in the week. Cleaning and visits had to move around it.

choices.label: Keep Saturday for family plans
choices.outcome_text: The familiar Saturday routine stayed. Your child looked for another way to spend time on the interest.

choices.label: Alternate club and family Saturdays
choices.outcome_text: The calendar began to change from week to week. There was time for both, but some club days were missed.

title: The book at cousin’s house
setup_text: A cousin borrowed your child’s favourite book and has not returned it. Your child wants it back before the next visit.

choices.label: Help your child ask for it
choices.outcome_text: A message went to the cousin. The book came back at the next opportunity, and the children still had other things to share.

choices.label: Ask the cousin’s parent yourself
choices.outcome_text: The grown-ups arranged the return. Your child got the book back without having to raise it directly.

choices.label: Wait until the next visit to bring it up
choices.outcome_text: The book stayed away a little longer. The request was made face to face when the families met.

title: The gift list
setup_text: Your child wants to buy holiday gifts for several cousins. The money set aside would cover either small gifts for everyone or one larger gift.

choices.label: Choose small gifts for everyone
choices.outcome_text: Several small parcels were wrapped. Each cousin received something, though none was the larger gift your child had imagined.

choices.label: Choose one larger shared gift
choices.outcome_text: One larger gift went to the cousins to use together. There were fewer parcels to open and a conversation about sharing it.

choices.label: Make some gifts and buy one
choices.outcome_text: The table filled with paper and tape as well as one bought gift. Making everything took time across several evenings.

title: A question after class
setup_text: Your child says a classroom rule feels unfair. The teacher has invited parents to discuss it, and your child wants to be heard.

choices.label: Help your child prepare a question
choices.outcome_text: Your child practised the question at home. The conversation at school gave everyone a little more to consider.

choices.label: Speak with the teacher first
choices.outcome_text: The grown-ups started the conversation. Your child heard what was discussed and could decide what to ask next.

choices.label: Invite the teacher and child to talk together
choices.outcome_text: The meeting included your child from the start. It took more arranging, and several views were heard.

title: Rain on a visiting day
setup_text: Rain has kept your child and a visiting cousin indoors. One wants a noisy game; the other would rather draw.

choices.label: Make room for each activity
choices.outcome_text: One corner became a drawing space and another held the game. The room was busy, and both children had something to do.

choices.label: Suggest taking turns choosing
choices.outcome_text: The afternoon moved between a game and drawing. Each child waited for a turn to lead.

choices.label: Find a game both children can shape
choices.outcome_text: Paper and a few household objects became a new game. It took a while to invent rules both children liked.

title: The last stretch to school
setup_text: Your child wants to walk the last short stretch to the school gate with a classmate. You usually walk all the way together.

choices.label: Walk nearby while the children lead
choices.outcome_text: The children led the way while a grown-up stayed nearby. The morning felt a little different without changing the whole journey.

choices.label: Keep walking to the gate together
choices.outcome_text: The familiar walk continued. Your child had company at the gate and time to talk with the classmate before class.

choices.label: Agree on a trial with the other family
choices.outcome_text: The two families discussed a short trial and a meeting point. It took planning before the new walk could begin.

title: A quiet hour
setup_text: Your child comes home tired and is invited to play outside. There is also a school activity to finish before tomorrow.

choices.label: Let your child rest before deciding
choices.outcome_text: A quiet break came first. The family looked at the activity later, with less time left for play.

choices.label: Make room for a short play visit
choices.outcome_text: A short visit outside broke up the afternoon. The school activity waited until everyone came back in.

choices.label: Ask your child to choose the order
choices.outcome_text: Your child helped arrange the afternoon. The family kept an eye on the clock as the evening got closer.

title: A call from a friend
setup_text: Your child wants a regular evening call with a school friend. The phone is shared and the same hour is usually family time.

choices.label: Set aside a short call time
choices.outcome_text: The friends had a regular time to talk. The shared phone was unavailable for a little while each evening.

choices.label: Keep calls to certain days
choices.outcome_text: The phone stayed free on other evenings. The friends had fewer calls but knew when to expect them.

choices.label: Ask your child to plan around family time
choices.outcome_text: Your child helped find a time that fitted the evening. The plan needed a little adjusting during the week.

title: The model on the table
setup_text: A school project is due soon. Your child wants to do it alone, but the materials and time are running short.

choices.label: Let your child lead while you stay nearby
choices.outcome_text: The model took its own shape, including a few uneven edges. Help was close if your child wanted it.

choices.label: Offer to prepare the materials together
choices.outcome_text: The family spent time getting the pieces ready. Your child still had decisions to make about the finished model.

choices.label: Ask the teacher about simpler materials
choices.outcome_text: A question went to school before the work continued. The project took a different shape with what was available.
